aim_error_deg.cite: ICGA skill model 1x — Archibald, Altman & Shoham, AAMAS 2010 Sec 2.2.1; adopted as canonical in rl-agent-program.md:840, units verified at :3837.  1x is CONSERVATIVE for a break.

tip_a_r.cite: intended 0 (no citation exists for deliberate sidespin on a break); sigma = ICGA sigma_a

tip_b_r.cite: mean = the shipped break gate pin, exp_e3_break.py:155-157 (HSV B.43 scenario 1, "stun (very slight draw)"); sigma = ICGA sigma_b

elevation_deg.cite: ICGA sigma_theta = 0.1 deg NOT applied — this ensemble models no cue elevation anywhere, and elevating the break alone would make it the only elevated stroke in the field

break.sequence: Halton radical inverse, bases 2 (speed), 3+5 and 7+11 (Box-Muller pairs for the normals); index = (seed * break-x strata + xi) * fullness strata + fi, so a disjoint rack-seed block moves the execution axes too
break.sequence_independence: NOT independent between batches. Halton here is deterministic and unscrambled, so disjoint seed blocks are disjoint index ranges of one sequence, with no randomisation and therefore no sampling distribution: "standard error" is undefined for them, not merely optimistic. A two-batch diff measures how far apart those two specified blocks land and bounds the integration error in NEITHER direction. Estimating an error needs several randomised QMC replicates (Owen scrambles or Cranley-Patterson shifts) with the spread taken across them — several, not one: R1 followup, not implemented. The rack axis is exempt — micro-gaps come from the kernel seeded generator.
